title: Manifold Partners with NEP Group for FPGA-accelerated Software-defined Production at Scale
body_html:
What Was Announced

Manifold has partnered with NEP Group to deliver FPGA-accelerated software-defined production at scale, a development that could potentially alter the dynamics of broadcast workflows. This collaboration aims to leverage the strengths of both parties to create a more efficient and scalable production environment. By integrating Manifold's expertise in software-defined workflows with NEP Group's extensive experience in live production, the partnership seeks to address the complexities and challenges associated with large-scale production.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The partnership between Manifold and NEP Group is significant because it highlights the growing importance of software-defined workflows in broadcast production. By utilizing FPGA acceleration, the solution can potentially reduce latency, increase processing power, and enhance overall system reliability. This, in turn, could lead to improved editorial control, faster turnaround times, and greater flexibility in responding to changing production requirements. Furthermore, the use of software-defined workflows can facilitate the automation of repetitive tasks, reduce manual errors, and enable more efficient resource allocation, ultimately streamlining the production process and allowing teams to focus on high-value tasks such as content creation and storytelling.

The integration of FPGA-accelerated processing can also enable the handling of complex tasks such as video encoding, decoding, and processing in real-time, which is critical for live production applications. Additionally, the solution's scalability and flexibility can support a wide range of production scenarios, from small-scale events to large-scale broadcasts, making it an attractive option for broadcasters and media companies looking to optimize their production workflows. The ability to easily scale up or down to meet changing production demands can also help reduce costs and improve resource utilization, making the solution more appealing to budget-conscious broadcasters.

Industry Context

The partnership between Manifold and NEP Group reflects the broader trend in the broadcast industry towards software-defined workflows and IP-based infrastructures. As the industry continues to evolve, there is a growing need for flexible, scalable, and efficient production solutions that can support a wide range of formats, resolutions, and delivery platforms. The use of FPGA acceleration and software-defined workflows is becoming increasingly common, with many vendors and broadcasters exploring the potential of these technologies to improve production efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance creativity. Comparable approaches can be seen in the adoption of SMPTE ST 2110 and AES67 standards for IP-based audio and video transport, which are designed to facilitate the transition to software-defined workflows and enable greater flexibility and interoperability in broadcast production.

The broadcast industry's shift towards software-defined workflows and IP-based infrastructures is also driven by the need to support emerging formats such as 4K, HDR, and immersive audio, which require more complex and processing-intensive workflows. The ability to easily integrate new technologies and formats into existing workflows is critical for broadcasters looking to stay ahead of the curve and deliver high-quality content to their audiences. As the industry continues to evolve, it is likely that we will see further adoption of software-defined workflows and IP-based infrastructures, as well as increased innovation in areas such as FPGA acceleration, artificial intelligence, and machine learning.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

For broadcast and media teams, the partnership between Manifold and NEP Group serves as a reminder of the importance of staying up-to-date with the latest technological advancements and innovations in software-defined workflows and IP-based infrastructures. As the industry continues to evolve, it is critical for teams to be aware of the potential benefits and challenges associated with adopting new technologies and workflows, and to carefully evaluate the implications for their specific production environments. Engineers and operations managers should take note of the potential for FPGA-accelerated software-defined production to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance creativity, and should consider the potential applications and benefits of this technology in their own workflows.
